featured_reviews.name: Mahbees Thayyil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this restaurant with eight of my friends, and all of us had a wonderful dining experience. From the moment we arrived, we were impressed by how welcoming and attentive the staff were. The service was excellent throughout our meal — friendly, prompt, and professional, which really added to the overall experience.

We ordered a variety of dishes including chicken biryani, chicken dum biryani, egg biryani, porotta, and fish. Every dish we tried was flavorful and well-prepared. The biryanis, in particular, were outstanding — aromatic, perfectly spiced, and served in generous portions. The chicken was tender and juicy, and the egg biryani had a lovely balance of flavors. The fish was also fresh and cooked beautifully with just the right amount of seasoning.

The only small area for improvement would be the porotta, which could have been a little softer. However, that didn’t take away from the overall great taste and quality of the food. We were all very satisfied with what we ordered.

Considering the quality, portion sizes, and service, the prices felt very reasonable. Overall, it was an enjoyable experience for our entire group, and I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for delicious food and great service.

featured_reviews.name: Owais Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Hidden Gem in Fort for Seafood Lovers

Tucked a little inside the lanes of Fort, this place has a very small and limited seating setup—it feels quite local and is not your typical family fine-dine spot.

But if you love fish, this place is a must-visit. The food is absolutely worth it—great taste and very affordable. I tried the Rawas Ghee Roast with Malabari Paratha, and it was a killer combo—perfectly cooked fish with rich, spicy flavors paired with soft, flaky paratha.

Overall, don’t go here for ambience—go for the food, and you won’t be disappointed.

featured_reviews.name: Rutesh Ajgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:

We ordered the Jumbo Surmai (0/5) and it was extremely disappointing. It was deep fried in what tasted like a Chinese-style masala, which completely ruined the flavor of the fish. The taste was not good at all.

The Prawns Ghee Roast (1/5) was also very average, and unfortunately, the prawns were not cleaned properly, which was quite off-putting. The Laccha Paratha was just okay.

Overall, not a satisfying dining experience and not somewhere I would revisit.

featured_reviews.name: Shivesh Bhatt
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let's start with the 40 minute wait. When you're made to wait that long, you naturally expect something rewarding at the end of it...The ambience was good, and after waiting so long to get a table, we were genuinely happy to finally be seated. The place is moderately expensive, and honestly, nobody mind paying a premium if the experience justifies it. Unfortunately, the service here was pathetic

My friend asked for a bottle of water and specifically requested one at normal temperature. Even after more than 30 minutes, it didn't arrive. When it finally did, they brought chilled water instead. I understand weekends are busy and service may take longer than usual, but taking that much time for a simple bottle of water is ridiculous

Not wanting to waste any more time, we ordered Masala Papad. When it arrived, it had no sev on it. Upon asking, we were casually told that they didn't have available. At the prices you're charging, are customers supposed to simply accept a poorer experience without question?

Then came the next masterpiece. One of my friends ordered a Diet Coke. After waiting more than 10 minutes, the waiter brought a regular Coke. At that point, all of us started laughing because it had become almost comical. When we asked whether they even had Diet Coke, he confidently said they did. The problem was that he had already opened the regular can before asking to change it.

Unfortunately, the experience didn't stop there. We ordered Tandoori Rotis, and the first round arrived burnt to the point that they looked like coal. We told the waiter and politely requested that the next be made properly. The second round arrived looking exactly the same. When we pointed it out, the waiter simply replied, "Weekend hai sir, ho jata hai"

For God's sake, man, we're here to enjoy our weekend too. Why are you ruining the experience?

Throughout the evening, we kept laughing at all the things that kept going wrong because otherwise it would have been frustrating. But when the bill arrived, I genuinely felt compelled to write this review. I rarely leave negative reviews and have never written one this harsh before, but this experience left me with no choice :,)

featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located at Colaba Causeway, this mughlai place is a pretty old and one of the legendary eateries which the city has to offer

The place has a royal ambiance but i believe they are definitely in a need of upgrade now.. especially the upper floors. The service is good.. initially it took a while for them to serve us as there was a huge corporate group having their party but once they had their attention to us.. they made sure that we are served well!

We went there for lunch, we ordered:
1) Roomali Roti: The roti was literally soft like a cushion and melts in your mouth, this is one of the best Roomali roti I have ever had.

2) Chicken Bhuna: Made on tawa, this boneless chicken bhuna was actually delicious. Chicken cooked was soft and melting in my mouth whereas the masala had right amount of spices to it and wasn't spicy which was to my liking!

3) Chicken Tikka Biryani: Usually the highlight of the restaurant, but to my surprise the biryani was better than what I had 1.5 years ago as it seems their chef has changed. The last time when I had it, the chicken was really dry and had been marinated in red color.. though it was charred well but was too dry! Whereas this time the tikka was properly marinated and grilled to the right amount leaving the chicken juicy and tender. The quantity served was good too. The rice i believe could have been more fluffier.

4) Sweet Fresh lime soda: The lemon concentrate at the bottom mixed with sugar and added soda.. mixed well.. definitely was refreshing but i wish they could add the fresh lemon juice for better taste.

Overall, a good place to have your fulfilling dinner.. the place had originally introduced to me by my mother.. though it might have changed over the time but still manages to have the same pull!

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.

Moving on we had the butter naan along with the chicken tikka masala. Another stellar combo. Hot, fluffy naans with perfectly spiced chicken tikka masala with that perfectly caramelised onion flavour, something you should definitely order.

Next we moved to the chicken biryani. It’s a light biryani. Not too oily not too heavily reliant on array of spices. Simple yet tasty. Perfect lunch is what I would say.

2) Although the floor plan ensured enough walking space (we were seated on table 10) the place seemed noisy. The speakers was loud. This made people speak louder. Expected a light music that enables peaceful meal experience.

3) Usually, both food & beverage menu is handed in the hand, in our case only the food menu was handed to us. The beverage menu was placed on the table.

4) The staff looked tired and overworked. We were requested for a beverage while the server was moving rather than stationary. Even when the glass was empty, we expected someone showing up checking on us if a refill was required.
The server brought the food and served the curry. However left without serving roti/naan. He left saying enjoy your food. Felt like I am in a hurry please help yourselves.

5) We ordered new item on the menu ‘beetroot kebab’. Was not that interesting. The filling overpowered the whole taste of beetroot.
Paneer lababdar had a different taste like the garlic had overpowered it.

In summary a LESS THAN AVERAGE experience.

This place excels by offering truly authentic, affordable, and incredibly satisfying North Indian and Punjabi vegetarian cuisine that tastes genuinely homemade.
​The food is the undisputed hero here. The Dal Makhani is rich and smoky, the Baingan Bharta is perfectly roasted, and the rotis are soft and fresh. Everything feels light, yet deeply flavorful, avoiding the heavy oiliness of typical restaurant fare. But the absolute, non-negotiable must-try is the Kheer. Served chilled and thick, it is quite simply the best finish to any meal and is worth the trip alone. The portion sizes are generous, offering fantastic value for money, especially with their thali options.
​However, be prepared for the realities of this beloved, long-running institution. The seating area is compact and the ambiance is simple—it’s clean, but very basic and constantly buzzing. Service is quick and efficient, but during peak hours, the wait time can be significant, and the staff can be rushed. Furthermore, the lack of modern amenities might deter some.
​Overall, Crystal earns a solid four stars. It loses a star only for the functional drawbacks (waiting time, limited space), but it gains five stars for its unparalleled food quality and value. It's an iconic Mumbai spot that delivers a warm, comforting hug in a bowl, perfect for a no-frills, delicious meal

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had lunch at Shalimar Hotel in Byculla and decided to try their Bheja Masala with Butter Naan. Dining alone sometimes helps you focus on the food instead of conversations, which in this case turned out to be a good thing.

The Bheja Masala was exceptionally well prepared, fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. It had a rich texture and balanced spices that paired wonderfully with the soft, buttery naan. Every bite felt satisfying without being overly heavy.

The ambience is pleasant and comfortable, making it a nice place to enjoy a relaxed meal. The restaurant is well known for its Mughlai cuisine and offers a wide variety of dishes for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians.

Whether you're visiting with family, friends, or simply looking for a good meal on your own, Shalimar Hotel is definitely worth a visit. Great food, good ambience, and a consistently enjoyable dining experience.
